placementGuidelines: VOLUNTEER-WEED, MANAGEABLE: a native North American perennial that self-invites into flower beds via an aggressive underground root system and will rob neighboring plants of water/nutrients if left unchecked - thin it out by pulling stalks by the base (use gloves) rather than trying to eradicate it outright, since a native perennial with real value doesn't need full removal. Positives worth keeping: fine, feathery dill-like foliage is a favorite cut-flower filler in vases with roses (crush a leaf to confirm ID - musky, non-licorice scent, unlike true fennel), and contained patches provide extra textural/wildlife cover at no cost. Pinch the top 2 in. of growing tips to force bushy, multi-branched growth for fuller cut sprays instead of one 6 ft. lanky spear. Do not fertilize it directly - keep phosphorus-heavy bloom boosters targeted at the base of desired companions only, since Dog Fennel's greedy roots will happily out-compete them for the boost. Rarely flowers until very late fall (insignificant yellowish-white clusters).
